title: Dice the food with a chef knife (Franka, operational-space control)
text: A tomato lies on a chopping board on a kitchen island; a chef knife lies on a knife rest beside the board. The tomato is scored on a grid: 2 planes across and 2 along it. Goal: pick up the knife and press its edge down through each scored plane (blade aligned with the plane — turn the blade 90 deg for the second set) to dice the tomato. It is diced once every plane has been pressed through and the pieces separate, all of them staying on the board.
success: Success, exactly: at the end of the run the tomato is in 9 separate pieces. All 12 scored joints between neighbouring cells of its 3 x 3 grid (6 for the planes across it, 6 for the planes along it) have been released [`pieces_count() >= 9`]. The centre (vertex-mean centroid) of every piece lies over the chopping board: within 0.30 m of the board's centre along its long side, within 0.13 m along its short side, and above the board's top surface (0.882 m above the floor). A joint releases, permanently, at the first instant all of these hold: the knife edge, at its point nearest the joint's cut point, is within 6 mm of the joint's plane and within 25 mm of the cut point horizontally along that plane; the blade face is within 15° of parallel to the plane; the edge is lower than the higher of the cut point's height and 1.5 mm above the board top; both pieces move under 0.10 m/s; and the knife rises no faster than 0.02 m/s. Not true at the start (one welded tomato).
